characters.name: Ajax
characters.description:
A **weathered man in his late fifties**, broad-shouldered but stooped, with close-cropped iron-grey hair, a salt-and-pepper beard kept short, and a pale scar running through his left eyebrow. His hands are scarred and knotted from years of rope and iron, and his pale blue eyes watch doorways before faces. He wears a heavy navy oilskin coat, a patched wool jersey, rubber-soled sea boots and a battered peaked cap.

He keeps the **Pale Light** on the southern rock, and carries himself like a man listening for footsteps.
characters.backstory:
He came to the coast fifteen years ago under another name, off a southern road he never speaks of. Before the Pale Light he was a **ship's pilot for the Brass & Tallow Company's predecessor**, and he signed his name to a harbour report that he knew was false. Men drowned afterwards. He took the lonely tower as penance and as hiding.

On the night the bell vanished he saw a **shuttered lantern signalling from the Drowned Stair** and a low boat moving without oars, and he has told no one, because the signal pattern was one he used to know. *If the bell's secret comes out, so does his.* He wants to find the bell before anyone else does, and he is not sure whether he wants to save it or bury it.

characters.name: Ajax
characters.description:
A **lean woman-of-few-words in her early thirties**, tall, with sharp cheekbones, a long dark braid pinned up under a knitted cap, and weather-reddened skin. She has ink-stained fingers and a habit of squinting as if into distance. She wears a long grey wool coat with brass buttons, fingerless gloves, a lamp-keeper's leather satchel and sturdy boots flecked with whitewash.

She keeps the **Old Light** on the north horn, as her family has for three generations.
characters.backstory:
She inherited the Old Light from her grandfather and mother, and with it a **logbook tradition**: every keeper writes what they see, and every keeper keeps quiet about what they cannot explain. Her family has always been close to the Chapel and the Net-Menders, and she grew up with the Widow's Bell as a lullaby.

That night, from the lamp room, she saw **the fog glow amber near the breakwater** and heard, just once, a muffled sound like a great hand laid over a bell mouth. Her mother's old logs mention the same thing, in a year the sexton's ledger skips. She is dutiful, stubborn and proud, and she is beginning to suspect that her family's quiet duty was never just about keeping a lamp lit.

npcs.name: Odalys Venn
npcs.description: A **brisk woman in her forties**, small and neat, with silver-streaked auburn hair in a tight bun, round wire spectacles and a perpetually ink-smudged cuff. She wears a dark double-breasted harbour-office coat with a tin badge and carries a leather folder.
npcs.backstory: Deputy to the Harbourmaster and the real author of the notice reading *no questions asked*. She fears a crime would invite the Company's inspectors and end the Office's authority. She is not corrupt, only frightened of disorder, and she keeps a private list of things she has chosen not to know.
npcs.relationships: She is wary of both Ajaxes and keeps the two straight with a pencilled chart on her wall. She leans on Brass & Tallow's goodwill for funding and quietly dislikes the Net-Menders' judgement talk.

npcs.name: Brannoch Teale
npcs.description: A **huge, slow-moving man of sixty-odd**, with a heavy white beard, a nose broken more than once, and hands like shovels. He wears a thick cable-knit jersey, a sealskin waistcoat and a woollen watch cap.
npcs.backstory: Elder of the Net-Menders' Guild and a fisherman since boyhood. He believes the bell was *kept, never owned*, and that the town's loss is a judgement. He privately knows his own father took coin for silence about the wreck that made the bell.
npcs.relationships: He respects the Old Light's keeper's family and distrusts the Pale Light's keeper as an outsider. He openly opposes the Company and the Harbourmaster's Office, and he is a regular at the Lantern & Eel despite himself.

npcs.name: Sexton IlsabetOrrow
npcs.description: An **elderly, tiny woman in her late seventies**, with thin white hair under a black lace cap, deeply lined face, cloudy but sharp grey eyes and a stoop from years of bending over ledgers. She wears a black wool dress, a long grey shawl and a ring of iron keys at her waist.
npcs.backstory: She has kept the Chapel of St. Orrin's records for fifty years. The **last page of the bell's ledger** has a name written in a hand that is not the vestry's, added the day before the bell vanished. She has told no one, afraid of what it would do to the town.
npcs.relationships: She trusts the Old Light's family more than anyone and is shy of the Pale Light's keeper. Brannoch Teale is her oldest friend and her oldest argument.

npcs.name: Cassian Marlowe-Reeve
npcs.description: A **polished man in his late thirties**, slim, clean-shaven, with slicked dark hair, warm brown eyes and a ready smile that does not quite reach them. He wears a well-cut charcoal city overcoat, a silk cravat, polished boots too good for the quay, and carries a silver-topped cane.
npcs.backstory: Local agent for the Brass & Tallow Company. He sincerely believes a steam-horn will save lives, and is quietly ashamed of the cruder methods his employers use. Someone in the Company is selling the bell, and he suspects it is his superior.
npcs.relationships: He courts the Harbourmaster's Office and is cordially loathed by the Net-Menders. He tries to befriend both keepers and is certain at least one is lying to him.

npcs.name: Wren Pellam
npcs.description: A **wiry girl of about fourteen**, freckled, with a tangle of sandy hair, scabbed knees and quick, watchful green eyes. She wears a too-large fisherman's jumper with rolled sleeves, patched trousers and bare or mud-caked feet.
npcs.backstory: An orphan who runs errands for the Lantern & Eel and sleeps in a net loft. She knows the smugglers' tunnels better than any adult, and that night she heard **wheels on the cobbles and a horse's feet muffled in sacking**. She tells no adult because she thinks she'll be blamed.
npcs.relationships: She is fond of the Lantern & Eel's landlady and is wary of officials. She will trust whichever keeper is kind to her first.

npcs.name: Maud Harrowgate
npcs.description: A **broad, ruddy woman in her fifties**, with curly grey-black hair tied in a red kerchief, strong forearms, a booming laugh and tired dark eyes. She wears a stained canvas apron over a wool dress and rolled sleeves.
npcs.backstory: Landlady of the Lantern & Eel, who hears every theory and sorts them by who pays. She has noticed a stranger's room paid in advance, and a **ship's name chalked on a slate that was later rubbed out**.
npcs.relationships: Mother figure to Wren, old friend of Brannoch, and creditor to half the quay. She keeps the peace between the Company's men and the Net-Menders by watering both their drinks.

npcs.name: Tobiah Crane
npcs.description: A **stooped, gaunt man in his seventies**, with a bald freckled head, drooping white moustache, milky left eye and trembling, rope-calloused hands. He wears a ragged brown apron, a faded cloth cap and an old rope-maker's leather wristguard.
npcs.backstory: The last rope-maker of the shuttered Cooperage. He made the bell's rope and knows the cut was made with a **blade he sharpened himself**, years ago, for a man he will not name.
npcs.relationships: He was once close to the Old Light's family and is terrified of the Pale Light's keeper's past. He will say nothing to the Harbourmaster's Office.
